title: Why Read the Puranas? The 18 Puranas and Their Benefits
desc: An introduction to the eighteen Puranas of Hindu tradition, who first taught them, what the verses promise readers, and a simple way to start reading.
alt: Palm-leaf manuscripts of the eighteen Puranas beside an oil lamp
caption: The eighteen Puranas: stories, rituals and teaching in one tradition.
intro: Hindu tradition counts **eighteen major Puranas** (the **Ashtadasa Puranas**). The **Brahma Purana** is first in the usual list, followed by the Padma, Vishnu, Vayu, Bhagavata, Narada, Markandeya, Agni and others. This post explains why people read them and how to begin.
takeaways: There are **18 major Puranas**; each mixes stories, geography, rituals, genealogies and teaching.
Tradition names a **first speaker and first listener** for each.
Verses promise **merit, wisdom and liberation** to those who listen with faith.
Start with **one story a week**, not a whole volume.

p: Each Purana is a large collection of **stories, sacred geography, rituals, genealogies and teaching**. Together they carry much of what Hindu tradition remembers about creation, gods, kings and sages.

Tradition gives each Purana a first speaker and first listener. For the **Brahma Purana**, the book says Brahma taught it to the sage **Marichi**. For the **Padma Purana**, it names **Svayambhuva Manu** as teaching Brahma.

A well-known verse in the introduction says that one who listens to the Puranas with faith pleases **Shiva and Vishnu together**. Another says the reader gains the merit of bathing at holy places. Another lists wishes fulfilled: a child for the childless, wealth for the seeker, learning for the student and liberation for the one who longs for it.

ol: Begin with **one story**, not a whole volume.
Read it with the question: **what is this telling me about how to live?**
Return on the **same day each week** so it becomes a habit.

p: We will publish **one Purana at a time, chapter by chapter**, as plain English retellings with images and a matching video where one exists. We stay close to the text but write in our own words.

faq.a: Tradition counts **eighteen major Puranas** (Ashtadasa Puranas), along with many minor ones.
The **Brahma Purana** is first in the usual list.

faq.q: Which Purana should a beginner read first?
faq.a: Any story-rich one works. Many readers begin with a single story from the **Bhagavata** or **Brahma Purana**, one a week.

note: This is an introduction in our own words, based on the introduction of a Telugu prose edition of the Puranas.
